# Signals & analyst evidence

Understand browser, behavioral, network, velocity, and identity evidence used in scoring and case investigation.

Source: [site documentation](https://web-production-c0739.up.railway.app/docs/signals) · platform revision `4b7879729687067d55fe230a0503385b205c0018`.

<a id="families"></a>

## Evidence families

| Family | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Browser & automation | Headless/framework indicators, capability inconsistencies, fingerprint spoofing, and evasion. |
| Behavior | Interaction absence, implausible timing/motion, replay patterns, and sample consistency. |
| Freshness | Timestamp, nonce, and request consistency evidence carried by complete telemetry. |
| Network | Observed IP, proxy/datacenter patterns, and available transport/browser consistency. |
| Velocity & credentials | Signup/checkout bursts, account reuse, and server-validated login outcomes. |
| Identity & payment | Shared device/IP/payment identifiers, account links, promo reuse, and fraud rings. |
| ML signals | Enterprise model signals where the deployed model has evidence available. |

Detection depends on available evidence, enabled rules, and plan access. A signal name is not a guarantee that every transport measurement exists behind every proxy. Preserve signal.description to inspect the actual observation rather than inferring a transport capability from the name alone.

<a id="login"></a>

## Supply real login outcomes

**typescript**

```typescript
const request = await bastion.buildRequest({
  event_type: 'login',
  account_id: 'customer_123',
});
// Send to your own login handler. That handler validates credentials.

// On the server, after your authentication provider completes:
const decision = await serverBastion.verify({
  ...request,
  context: {
    event_type: 'login',
    account_id: authenticatedOrAttemptedAccountId,
    login_succeeded: credentialsWereValid,
  },
});
```

The final two values above are outputs of your server-side authentication logic. A client-provided login_succeeded value is not trusted. Keeping the result absent when it is unknown is preferable to inventing an outcome. Credential-stuffing evidence uses verified server outcomes where available.

<a id="analyst"></a>

## Investigate with the fraud analyst

The dashboard analyst uses account events, rule evidence, identity links, and the newer anti-bot signals to answer distinct questions about the case. Graph access and ring evidence are plan-gated. Use it to understand observations and next steps, then record your actual review outcome.

> **Evidence has limits**
>
> Shared IPs and devices can occur in legitimate households or networks. Behavioral absence can occur with short sessions or assistive tools. Review multiple observations and customer context; a 0–100 risk score is not a calibrated probability of fraud.

- [Open Fraud Analyst](https://web-production-c0739.up.railway.app/dashboard/analyst) — Investigate tenant account evidence.
- [Decision policy](decisions.md) — Separate observations from enforcement.
